brief.title: Driver Dispatch & Proof-of-Delivery Platform
business_goals: Automate rider assignment based on proximity and current load to improve efficiency.
Reduce 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks through robust proof-of-delivery (photo + signature/OTP).
Ensure real-time order status updates flow back to the existing Unicommerce Order Management System.
Prevent riders from going off-route unnoticed to improve accountability and customer service.
Enable automatic reattempts for failed deliveries with clear reason codes.
Go live before the next major sale event (within approximately 10 weeks).

stakeholders.name: Karan Malhotra
concerns: Minimizing 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks

stakeholders.name: Neha Iyer
concerns: Managing project scope (e.g., batch routing out of scope)

stakeholders.name: Ravi Kumar
concerns: Rider mobile app functionality (route display, offline capability)
App performance on low-end Android devices
Standardized process for failed deliveries and reattempts

stakeholders.name: Sameer Qureshi
concerns: Scalability of dispatch engine (10-second assignment at peak)

constraints: Auto-assignment must consider both distance and current rider load.
Rider mobile app must work with patchy network, queuing updates offline and syncing when signal returns.
Proof of delivery requires a photo and either a signature or customer-entered OTP.
OTP should be sent automatically via SMS when the rider is within 500 meters of the drop location.
Customer-facing tracking link needs to update rider's location at least every 30 seconds.
Existing Google Maps Platform contract is to be used for maps and routing.
Failed deliveries require reason codes and automatically trigger up to two reattempts the next day.
The system must integrate with the existing Unicommerce Order Management System (not replace it).
Dispatch engine must assign a rider within 10 seconds, even at peak (9,000 deliveries/day).
Rider app must run acceptably on low-end Android devices (riders use their own phones).
Project must be live before the next big sale event (approximately 10 weeks out).
Budget capped at 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.
out_of_scope: Batch route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries (e.g., solving the best order to visit 40 stops); only single-order assignment for this phase.

stories.title: Automatic Order Assignment
stories.i_want: the system to automatically assign orders to riders based on proximity and current load
stories.so_that: I can optimize delivery efficiency and reduce manual effort

acceptance_criteria.given: a new order is received and available riders are online
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the order for assignment
acceptance_criteria.then: a rider is assigned

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple available riders
acceptance_criteria.when: the system assigns an order
acceptance_criteria.then: the system prioritizes assignment to the rider closest to the pickup location, then by the rider with the lower current load

stories.notes: Performance requirements R-022 and R-023 will be handled as separate non-functional requirements or performance stories.

stories.title: Capture Photo Proof of Delivery
stories.i_want: to capture a photo as proof of delivery
stories.so_that: I can document successful deliveries and reduce disputes

acceptance_criteria.given: I am at the customer's location and ready to complete a delivery
acceptance_criteria.when: I select the "Capture Photo" option
acceptance_criteria.then: the device camera is activated, allowing me to take a photo

acceptance_criteria.given: a photo has been captured
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to mark the delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the photo is stored as part of the delivery record

stories.title: Capture Signature Proof of Delivery
stories.i_want: to capture a customer signature as proof of delivery
stories.so_that: I can document successful deliveries and reduce disputes

acceptance_criteria.given: I am at the customer's location and ready to complete a delivery
acceptance_criteria.when: I select the "Capture Signature" option
acceptance_criteria.then: a signature pad is displayed, allowing the customer to sign

acceptance_criteria.given: a signature has been captured
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to mark the delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the signature is stored as part of the delivery record

stories.title: Rider Captures and Validates OTP
stories.i_want: to capture and validate a customer-entered OTP for proof of delivery
stories.so_that: I can securely verify the customer's identity and complete the delivery

acceptance_criteria.given: the customer has received an OTP
acceptance_criteria.when: I enter the customer-provided OTP into the app
acceptance_criteria.then: the system validates the OTP and displays a success or failure message

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid OTP is entered
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to mark the delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the OTP verification is recorded as part of the delivery record

acceptance_criteria.given: an invalid OTP is entered
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to mark the delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the system prevents completion and prompts for re-entry or an alternative POD method

stories.notes: Requires 'Customer Receives OTP via SMS' (S-014) to be completed first.

stories.title: Mandatory Proof of Delivery Enforcement
stories.i_want: the system to enforce proof of delivery (photo and either signature or OTP) before marking a delivery complete
stories.so_that: 'item not received' disputes are minimized and delivery accountability is ensured

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.when: neither a photo nor a signature/OTP has been captured
acceptance_criteria.then: the system prevents completion and displays a message prompting for the required proof

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider has captured a photo and either a signature or a valid OTP
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the system allows the delivery to be marked complete

stories.notes: This story is dependent on S-002 (Photo POD), S-003 (Signature POD), and S-004 (OTP POD).

stories.title: Receive Orders from Unicommerce
stories.i_want: the system to receive new order details from Unicommerce
stories.so_that: orders are automatically available for dispatch without manual entry

acceptance_criteria.given: the Unicommerce integration is active
acceptance_criteria.when: a new order is created or updated in Unicommerce
acceptance_criteria.then: the order details are successfully received by the dispatch system within 30 seconds

stories.title: Alert Operations on Route Deviation
stories.i_want: to receive alerts when a rider goes off-route
stories.so_that: I can intervene quickly to ensure accountability and customer service

acceptance_criteria.given: the system has detected a route deviation for a rider
acceptance_criteria.when: the deviation persists for a predefined duration (e.g., 5 minutes)
acceptance_criteria.then: the system generates an alert (e.g., dashboard notification, email) for operations personnel

stories.notes: Requires 'Rider Location Tracking & Deviation Detection' (S-015) to be completed first.

stories.title: Customer Real-time Tracking
stories.i_want: my tracking link to show the rider's location updated frequently
stories.so_that: I can accurately anticipate my delivery

acceptance_criteria.given: I am viewing my delivery tracking link
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider is en route
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider's location on the map updates at least every 30 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: the system is using Google Maps Platform
acceptance_criteria.when: rider location data is received
acceptance_criteria.then: it is accurately displayed on the customer tracking link

stories.notes: Requires 'Rider Location Tracking & Deviation Detection' (S-015) to be completed first.

stories.title: Rider Daily Route Display
stories.i_want: the mobile application to display my sequence of stops for the day on a map
stories.so_that: I can efficiently manage my deliveries

acceptance_criteria.given: I have logged into the rider mobile application
acceptance_criteria.when: I view my assigned deliveries
acceptance_criteria.then: a map displays the sequence of stops for all my assigned deliveries using Google Maps Platform, showing the assigned route between them

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on a delivery
acceptance_criteria.when: I check my route
acceptance_criteria.then: the map highlights my current position relative to the planned route and upcoming stops

stories.notes: This story assumes the route is provided by the system (not optimized by the app). Requires 'Automatic Order Assignment' (S-001) to be completed first.

stories.title: Rider Selects Failed Delivery Reason
stories.i_want: to select a predefined reason code for failed deliveries
stories.so_that: operations can understand the issue and manage reattempts effectively

acceptance_criteria.given: I am unable to complete a delivery
acceptance_criteria.when: I mark the delivery as failed
acceptance_criteria.then: the app presents a list of predefined reason codes (e.g., "Customer Not Available", "Wrong Address", "Refused Delivery")

acceptance_criteria.given: I select a reason code
acceptance_criteria.when: I confirm the failed delivery
acceptance_criteria.then: the selected reason code is recorded with the delivery status

stories.title: Automatic Reattempt Scheduling
stories.i_want: the system to automatically trigger and schedule reattempts for failed deliveries
stories.so_that: I can ensure customers eventually receive their orders without manual intervention

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery is marked as failed for the first time
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the failed delivery
acceptance_criteria.then: a reattempt is automatically scheduled for the next day, marked as the first reattempt

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery is marked as failed for the second time (first reattempt failed)
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the failed delivery
acceptance_criteria.then: a reattempt is automatically scheduled for the next day, marked as the second and final reattempt

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery has failed twice (second reattempt failed)
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the failed delivery
acceptance_criteria.then: the system marks the delivery for return to the hub and prevents further reattempts

stories.notes: Requires a story for marking deliveries as failed (e.g., S-010, which is not provided but implied) and 'Automatic Order Assignment' (S-001) for re-assignment.

stories.title: Offline Data Queuing & Sync
stories.i_want: to perform delivery actions (e.g., status updates, POD capture) even with patchy or no network connectivity
stories.so_that: my work is not interrupted, and data is reliably synchronized when connectivity returns

acceptance_criteria.given: I am in an area with no network connectivity
acceptance_criteria.when: I mark an order as 'picked up' or 'attempted delivery'
acceptance_criteria.then: the app stores the action locally, visually indicates offline mode, and allows me to proceed with other tasks

acceptance_criteria.given: I have captured a photo or signature for POD while offline
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to complete the delivery
acceptance_criteria.then: the app stores the POD data locally and queues it for synchronization

acceptance_criteria.given: I have queued offline updates (status changes, POD data)
acceptance_criteria.when: network connectivity is restored
acceptance_criteria.then: the app automatically and silently syncs all queued updates to the server

acceptance_criteria.given: I am using the app with patchy network
acceptance_criteria.when: I perform actions
acceptance_criteria.then: the app remains responsive and functional, queuing data as needed without blocking my workflow

stories.title: Low-End Device Compatibility
stories.i_want: the mobile application to run acceptably on low-end Android devices
stories.so_that: I can use my existing phone without needing an upgrade

acceptance_criteria.given: I am using a low-end Android device (e.g., specified minimum RAM/processor)
acceptance_criteria.when: I use the rider mobile application
acceptance_criteria.then: the app launches within 5 seconds and key functions (e.g., viewing orders, capturing POD) respond within 2 seconds

issues: The second acceptance criterion regarding prioritization ("prioritizes assignment to the rider closest to the pickup location, then by the rider with the lower current load") is ambiguous. It's unclear if this is a strict two-step process or a weighted combination, and how ties are broken.
The story might be too large, as combining two distinct assignment criteria (proximity and load) can involve significant logic and edge cases.
AC2.then has no observable outcome verb
reviews.fix_instructions: Clarify the exact prioritization logic in the second acceptance criterion. For example, specify if it's a strict primary/secondary sort, or a combined scoring function. Define tie-breaking rules. Consider splitting the story into smaller parts, e.g., "Assign by Proximity" and "Assign by Load," then a separate story for "Combined Assignment Logic."

issues: The story has an explicit dependency on "S-014: Customer Receives OTP via SMS" which is not provided in the list of stories. This violates the 'Independent' criterion.

gaps.description: The backlog story S-006 'Receive Orders from Unicommerce' only covers receiving orders. There is no explicit story in the backlog to cover sending real-time order status updates back to Unicommerce, which is a key business goal and covered by requirement R-006.
gaps.suggested_question: Is there a separate story or a plan to cover sending real-time order status updates *from* our system *to* Unicommerce, as per R-006?

gaps.description: The backlog story S-004 'Rider Captures and Validates OTP' focuses on the rider's interaction with the OTP. However, the brief and requirements (R-016, R-017) specify that the system should *automatically send* the OTP via SMS to the customer when the rider is within 500 meters. This automated sending mechanism is not explicitly covered in the backlog.
gaps.suggested_question: S-004 covers OTP capture and validation by the rider. Is there a story planned to cover the automated sending of the OTP via SMS to the customer, as specified in R-016 and R-017?

gaps.description: Several critical non-functional requirements, such as the project timeline (R-010), dispatch engine performance (R-022, R-023), and budget (R-025), are present in the requirements but do not have explicit corresponding stories or tracking mechanisms mentioned in the backlog summary. While some NFRs are linked, these overarching project constraints are not.
gaps.suggested_question: How are the non-functional requirements for project timeline (R-010), dispatch engine performance (R-022, R-023), and budget (R-025) being tracked and ensured within the backlog or project plan?

gaps.description: The brief does not list 'Customer' or 'Customer Support Representative' as a stakeholder, despite the system having significant customer-facing features like real-time tracking (R-018, S-008) and OTP delivery (R-016, R-017, S-004). Their perspective is crucial for defining and validating the user experience of these features.
gaps.suggested_question: Given the customer-facing features like tracking and OTP, should we consider adding 'Customer' or 'Customer Support Representative' as a stakeholder to ensure their needs and experience are adequately represented?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog generally provides good coverage for most functional requirements and business goals, particularly in areas like automatic rider assignment, proof of delivery mechanisms, failed delivery handling, and core rider app functionality. However, there are notable gaps concerning the explicit coverage of sending real-time order status updates to Unicommerce and the automated sending of OTP SMS to customers. Additionally, while critical non-functional requirements like project timeline, budget, and dispatch engine performance are stated, their explicit representation or tracking within the backlog is not evident. The customer, a key user of several features, is also not listed as a direct stakeholder.
